claims.statement: For shipped used EEE to avoid WEEE treatment, EU rules require direct-reuse documentation, item-level functionality tests and records, a non-waste declaration, and protective packaging; missing proof can trigger a presumption of illegal waste shipment.
A substantial modification can make the modifier liable as manufacturer, while repairs not amounting to substantial modification are excluded from that specific manufacturer treatment.
Poland's 1.6 million-plus microinstallations and a documented 10-15-year inverter life support a growing replacement base.
JRC reports module refurbishment can cost more than new production, warranty returns are about 0.048% in the first decade and around 0.2% later, and expected module life is roughly 30 years.
IEA PVPS describes module repair as underexplored, with few commercial services and incompletely established assurance practices.
SecondSol already serves over 60000 users with more than 250000 spare parts plus testing, repair, auctions, logistics, and recycling, closely matching the frozen offer.
SMA can ship a comparable latest-portfolio replacement within 48 hours, reducing scarcity for technically replaceable legacy inverters.
The defensible Polish niche, if any, is obsolete off-warranty equipment where documented fitment avoids redesign and neither OEM supply nor SecondSol inventory solves the job.

contrary_evidence: A scaled European incumbent already offers the complete marketplace and service stack.
Cheap new modules and long module life weaken reclaimed-module turnover.
OEM repowering and warranty replacement remove some of the most valuable failures from the open market.
Waste-status and product-liability evidence must be established item by item.
